title: Project 4 · Read and validate local tasks
prompt: Row, TaskItem, LoadResult and two row readers are supplied. Write public static async Task<LoadResult> LoadAsync(IRowReader reader). Read the rows once. A row is valid when its Id is a whole number greater than 0 and its Title is not empty. Return a LoadResult with Ok true, an empty Error, and the valid rows as tasks that are not done, in order. Reading no valid rows is still a success with an empty list. When the reader throws InvalidOperationException, return Ok false, an empty list of tasks, and the Error "unavailable".
hints: There are two kinds of bad news here: a reader that fails, and a row that is not valid. Which one makes Ok false?
Only the failed read is a failure. An invalid row is skipped and the load still succeeds.
Await the read in a try and return the failed result from catch (InvalidOperationException). Then convert the rows, using int.TryParse for the Id.
checks: Run(new MemoryRows(Rows("1|Pack", "2|Ship"))).Tasks.SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(1, "Pack", false), new TaskItem(2, "Ship", false) })
Run(new MemoryRows(Rows("x|Pack", "0|Zero", "3|", "4|Label"))).Tasks.SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(4, "Label", false) })
checkLabels: Two valid rows must become two tasks that are not done, in order.
A successful load must have Ok true and an empty Error.
Rows with a bad Id or an empty Title must be skipped without failing the load.
Reading no rows is a success with an empty list.
An unavailable reader must give Ok false and the Error "unavailable".
A failed load must still carry an empty list of tasks.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Reports a load with no valid rows as a failure.
Converts every Id with int.Parse and never checks the rows.

feedback: Separate the two questions: did the read itself fail, and which rows are valid? Only the first one decides Ok.
